contract: construct(n) -> a word over the symbols 1..n, given as a string of the digits 1..n or a list of integers; the evaluator passes this task's n. Valid when every permutation of 1..n occurs as n consecutive symbols (every window is checked). Score: the length of the word, minimized; at most n * n! symbols.
notes: Independent exact verifier over all windows of the word. The published record construction for every task was scored with this evaluator and reproduces the published value exactly (validation/human-results/frontier_combinatorics.json). The seed is the classic recursive construction of length 1! + ... + n!; unit tests check the known minimal lengths 9, 33 and 153 for n = 3, 4, 5.
protocol_description: Locally implemented evaluator with recorded reference checks; consult the task-specific tests and evidence for their exact scope. This label alone does not establish reproduction of the paper's full experiment.
name: Shortest superpermutation on seven symbols
description: Write the shortest word over the symbols 1 to 7 that contains every one of the 5040 permutations of 1..7 as seven consecutive symbols. The shortest known word has 5905 symbols (A. Teodorescu, August 2026) and the best published lower bound is 5884.
paper_metric: Local protocol; see candidate contract and source adaptation notes

sources.locator: Superpermutators mailing list, 18 August 2026: A. Teodorescu posts four length-5905 superpermutations for n = 7 (two distinct up to symmetry) found with G. Egan's PermutationChains.c and KernelFinder.c; A. Balint and S. Street confirm that they contain all 5040 permutations.
G. Egan's page: the previous record 5906 (Egan and Houston, 27 February 2019), its word, and the search programs.
R. Houston (2014), Tackling the minimal superpermutation problem.
Anonymous 4chan poster, R. Houston, J. Pantone and V. Vatter (2018): lower bound n! + (n-1)! + (n-2)! + n - 3, which is 5884 for n = 7.
OEIS A180632 (minimal superpermutation lengths): a(7) <= 5906 recorded in 2019.

limitations: The 5905 record was announced on a mailing list and checked there by several members; it has no peer-reviewed publication yet.
A lower bound of 5898 was also claimed on the same list in August 2026 without review; the published lower bound remains 5884.

The record construction is public, so a candidate can reproduce the record by embedding it; the score measures the returned object, not the search that produced it, and only a strictly smaller score than the best known value is a new result.
Candidate Python runs inside the evaluator process as trusted research code; the evaluator recomputes every property of the returned object exactly and trusts nothing the candidate reports.

state_of_the_art.comparability: Same object and objective: a word over 1..7 containing all 5040 permutations as contiguous blocks, shortest length. The posted word (first attachment) scores 5905 (valid) with this evaluator; Egan's 2019 word scores 5906.

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Determine the minimal length of a superpermutation on seven symbols: a word containing each of the 5040 permutations of 1..7 as a contiguous block.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: The minimal superpermutation problem is a well-known open problem in combinatorics on words. The conjecture that 1! + 2! + ... + n! is minimal failed in 2014, exact values are known only up to n = 5, and the lower-bound question is tied to Hamiltonian paths in Cayley graphs of the symmetric group; for seven symbols the gap between the lower bound 5884 and the best constructions is open.
